We need to see if the agent attempted to resolve the issue before transferring. The policy says: transfer only if request cannot be handled within scope of actions. For NQNU5R, the user wanted to cancel. The agent checked reservation details, saw flights were on May 13-14, which are in the past relative to current time May 15. According to policy: If any portion of the flight has already been flown, the agent cannot help and transfer is needed. The agent does not have a tool to check flight status (whether flight has flown). There's a tool get_flight_status. The agent did not call get_flight_status for the flights in NQNU5R to see if they have flown. The agent assumed that because dates are past, some portion may have flown, but need to verify. The policy says: "If any portion of the flight has already been flown, the agent cannot help and transfer is needed." The agent must make sure the rules apply before calling the API! For cancellation, the agent must obtain reason and ensure that if any portion flown, cannot cancel. The agent should check flight status to see if flown. The agent did not attempt to resolve by checking flight status; they directly transferred. So the suspicion: agent did not attempt to resolve the issue with the user before transferring them to a human agent for reservation NQNU5R. Is that true? The agent could have used get_flight_status to see if flights have flown. They didn't. So they didn't attempt to resolve via available tools. Therefore the suspicion is confirmed.
